title: New deal: discovery follow-up
summary: First substantive call on a new deal. The CRM record is empty. The customer names a signer and agrees to a demo, but only estimates the budget.
showcases: Safe autonomous write: an explicitly named signer and an accepted meeting time
Uncertain information preserved but routed to review: a hedged budget estimate
What Grounded knows vs what it writes: current vendor spend is heard but is not a budget

turns.text: Thanks for making time, Thandiwe and Florian. Last time we left off on dispatch automation. Where do things stand on your side?
Good timing, actually. Leadership wants the dispatch backlog fixed before peak season, so this is now a priority project.
From the systems side, the open question is the warehouse integration. We pay about $80K a year for the routing tool we have today, and it doesn't talk to anything else.
That's helpful context. On budget for this project, have you landed on a number yet?
Not formally. We're probably looking at something around $100K, but finance still has to bless a number.
Understood. Whose signature goes on the contract itself?
That would be Rosalind Achebe, our COO. She signs every vendor contract at this size.
Great. Could we get Florian and your dispatch leads together for a technical demo? I have Thursday at 2 Eastern open.
Thursday at 2 is fine by me.
Same here. Send the invite to both of us and I'll loop in the dispatch leads.

budget.why: "Probably looking at something around $100K" plus "finance still has to bless a number" is hedged (and arguably conditional). Grounded should keep ~$100K with the quote but must not write it.
risks: If the classifier labels the $80K vendor spend INDIRECT instead of NONE, the two budget candidates conflict. The field is still ASK, with the later $100K value.
If the extractor doesn't emit the $80K vendor spend at all, the ledger simply won't show it (TEST recall of such context was 6/23).

decisionMaker.why: The customer explicitly names the person who signs vendor contracts, in answer to "whose signature goes on the contract". Phrased as signing, not "needs to approve", which is a known classification weakness.
risks: The role could be extracted as "Chief Operating Officer". Display differs, but policy equality and the action are unaffected (empty CRM).

nextMeeting.why: The seller proposes Thursday at 2 Eastern, and both customers accept. The call is Tuesday 2026-11-10, so Thursday is 2026-11-12, and "at 2" reads 14:00. meeting-v1 verifies the weekday and the time.
risks: The timezone may be extracted as "ET" or "Eastern". Display only; it's ignored in comparisons.
